what_went_wrong: Search pulled Latin American investment pages and the draft padded half the answer with LatAm rental-yield stats nobody asked for, while giving no transaction-cost percentage or current mortgage rate and saying the current location was 'not provided' despite Brooklyn being set.
great_answer_would: Stay on the Brooklyn decision: rent, ~8-10% round trip vs ~7.3% rates, the already-own and 5+ year exceptions, and keep cash liquid for visa proof and deposits.
notes: Core verdict (rent, 5+ year break-even, transaction costs) is right and up front; the 'Buy only if you have significant existing equity' line half-captures the already-own exception. Ending by telling him to run a calculator is generic.

hallucinations.claim: 84% of purchases happen on smartphones
hallucinations.why: Precise share from a seller blog, unscoped (which countries, which year) and unverifiable; presented as fact

what_went_wrong: The draft got 'Brazil is the only country' right but then hedged on Mercado Libre ('you would need to check local market share reports for names like Mercado Libre to confirm') instead of stating what is well known, and gave no dates, no shelved-expansion context and no other local players.
great_answer_would: State plainly that Mercado Libre dominates (18 countries, own logistics and Mercado Pago), list Shopee/Magalu/Casas Bahia/Shein in Brazil and Falabella in Chile/Peru/Colombia, and note the paused 2023 Colombia/Chile launches.
notes: Central fact correct ('Brazil is the only country in South America with a dedicated Amazon marketplace'); the smartphone stat is filler that does not answer 'what do people use instead'.

what_went_wrong: Numbers are all right; it only omits the caveat that a $5 gap is noise and that the package's own taxes/resort fees and cancellation terms decide it, and the lead line is repeated in the body.
great_answer_would: Add one line saying $5 is noise and to check whether the package excludes taxes/resort fees and how cancellation compares.
notes: $2,395 vs $2,400 (separate by $5), $106.40/night, $1,170.40 hotel, $2,520.40 total, package cheaper by $120.40: all correct, 11 nights used, flight not taxed.

great_answer_would: Cut the restated final sentence to one line and add a gas-price sensitivity line.

hallucinations.claim: "you would take a standard nightly rate and apply a 30-50% discount"
hallucinations.why: Asserted as typical with no source; the sheet's range is 25-40%, so it is roughly right but unsupported.

what_went_wrong: Search returned only two thin sources, so the pricing half has no Florianópolis figure, no seasonality and no 90-day temporada point; the rating half is correct but misses that 4.6 is below Airbnb's compressed norm.
great_answer_would: Add the grade-compression caveat and give a concrete monthly range for a 2-bedroom (about R$5,000-8,000 furnished in Campeche/Lagoa), the high-season (Dec-Feb) carve-out and the 90-day temporada rule.
notes: Correctly names QuintoAndar and Zap Imóveis as comp sources and the discount range is close to the sheet; honest that it found no local prices. Short and direct, fitting the asker's style.

hallucinations.claim: "If you are running a small model on an 80GB A100, there is no benefit to quantizing"
hallucinations.why: Contradicts its own throughput point: decode is bandwidth-bound, so 4-bit still raises tokens per second even with VRAM headroom.

hallucinations.claim: "Models with very low parameter counts (under 7B) tend to degrade significantly"
hallucinations.why: Overstates the threshold; 7B-class models lose little at 4-bit, the sharp losses are below ~3B.

what_went_wrong: Facts mostly right (2 bytes to 0.5 bytes, 70B ~140 GB to ~40 GB, group sizes 64/128, sub-4-bit collapse), but it is long and heading-heavy for 'keep it short', has a typo ('a s-bit range') and an incoherent example ('a model that is 40GB on a 24GB GPU').
great_answer_would: Compress to five sentences and add the rule that a bigger 4-bit model beats a smaller 16-bit one at the same memory, plus that prefill gains less than decode.
notes: Best arithmetic of the three; correctly notes group-wise scaling and per-parameter overhead. No mention of KV cache/activations staying 16-bit.
